metadata.case_name: CHEUNG SZE KUEN v. WONG CHI CHEUNG AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: lacerations to the face and neck / scarring of the face and neck
source: the Plaintiff in evidence said that he also suffered lacerations to the face and neck and scratches to the leg.
the Plaintiff certainly has noticeable scars on the face and neck
scarring of the face and neck which is noticeable although not disfiguring.

injuries.description: fracture of the right wrist of the type known as a "Colles" fracture
source: the principal injury he sustained was a fracture of the right wrist of the type known as a "Colles "' fracture.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture at wrist or hand level

injuries.description: shoulder injury / weakness of the right shoulder
source: the comparatively brief medical reports from Princess Margaret Hospital also mention a shoulder injury, of which the Plaintiff only complained about a year later
Dr. Hodgson, who gave evidence, confirmed that he believed they were caused by the accident as was also the shoulder injury, and I accept that evidence.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of unspecified muscle, fascia or tendon at shoulder or upper arm level

source: the Plaintiff in evidence said that he also suffered lacerations to the face and neck and scratches to the leg.
these latter injuries are not mentioned in the hospital reports at all although they are in a "Medical Enquiry Form" dated 11th March 1983
injuries.icd_description: Abrasion of other or unspecified parts of lower leg

manifestations.description: permanent weakness and deformity of the right wrist
scarring of the face and neck which is noticeable although not disfiguring
loss of strength in the right arm (right-hand grip of about 70 lbs. to his left-hand grip of about 85 to 100 lbs.)
wasting of muscle in the right arm
cannot carry heavy weights, or even moderate weights over a prolonged period, and in particular cannot carry a tray with the palm uppermost
now effectively prevented from pursuing any occupation which involves lifting heavy weights

treatments_received: admitted to Princess Margaret Hospital where he remained for three days during which a plaster-of-Paris cast was applied and he was then transferred to Yan Chai Hospital for a further week, before being discharged.
about two weeks later he was re-admitted for a further reduction of the fracture as the fragments of bone had moved, and had a new cast for a month.
attended physiotherapy and occupational therapy clinics
attended a bonesetter in respect of his shoulder injury

losses.description: scarring of the face and neck which is noticeable although not disfiguring.
permanent weakness and deformity of the right wrist

cannot return to his pre-accident employment as a waiter as he can no longer carry heavy weights, or even moderate weights over a prolonged period, and in particular cannot carry a tray with the palm uppermost.
